threads.body: Weaver's emitted value is `log`, not `event`, as shown by the regenerated Google and Bedrock findings in this PR. Listing `event` here gives an incorrect account of the persisted `signal_type` values; it should also clarify that resource advice has no concrete signal name.

 @dataclass(frozen=True)
 class Finding:
-    """One thing weaver said, independent of how often it said it.
+    """One thing weaver said about one signal, however often it said it.
 
     ``context`` is kept serialised so two findings with the same message about
     different attributes stay apart, and so a finding is hashable.
+
+    ``signal_type`` and ``signal_name`` are what weaver stamps on every piece
+    of advice — the span, metric, event or resource it was checking. Advice
+    about an attribute carries the signal that held it, so a finding always
+    says where to go and look.

threads.body: The documented signal kinds and resource behavior do not match the generated format: this PR emits `signal_type: "log"` in the Google/Bedrock data, and the new resource test retains `signal_type: "resource"` while omitting only `signal_name`. As written, consumers could incorrectly reject `log` or expect resource findings to have neither field.
